newsitem.title: UK: UK regulator relaxes Mercury licence.
newsitem.headline: UK regulator relaxes Mercury licence.

text.p: British telecoms regulator Don Cruickshank on Friday relaxed the licence of Britain's second biggest telephone company -- Cable and Wireless's Mercury division.

Under the licence changes, Cruickshank said he had lifted a number of restrictions that date back to 1984, bringing Mercury's licence further into line with those of other non-dominant telecom companies.
While the watchdog will continue to prevent anti-competitive behaviour, he said he was now moving away from detailed prescriptive regulation.
Mercury welcomed the move, saying it allowed the company greater pricing flexibility and the chance to offer customers more specific services.
"Our customers -- particularly those who are national callers -- will be the winners," said Peter Howell-Davies, Mercury's chief executive.
Mercury's licence will be reviewed further later this year, with a view to propose modifications to bring it further into line with the "slimline" licences of smaller telecom companies.
